title: Casper and the Border
premise: Oscar Sterling, a freelance interpreter who cleans up the language of missions no government will own, receives a calendar invite from his dead handler, Casper, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at the border town of Vellmar. The meeting pulls him into an extraction operation: smuggle out Ilse Brandt, a defector carrying proof that the peace delegation Oscar serves was built to fail. As Oscar uncovers that Casper faked his death and that Ilse may be deliberate bait to flush out the mole inside the delegation, he must choose between exposing the inheritance of lies he's been translating all along or surviving it. In the end, Oscar lets himself be captured to pass the real evidence through Ilse, burning his identity so the truth crosses the border even if he doesn't.
about_author: Odile Vasquez is the pen name of a former NGO field translator who spent six years working border corridors in Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose job is to make other people's words sound survivable.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Interpreting a doomed ceasefire session in Geneva, Oscar notices the delegation's language has been pre-sabotaged. That night, a calendar invite arrives from Casper, his handler who died three weeks ago, for tomorrow, 09:00, Vellmar. The emotional beat is cold dread: grief weaponized into curiosity.

chapters.title: Vellmar
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Oscar goes to the border town against every instinct and finds not Casper but a dead drop containing Ilse Brandt's file and a burner phone that rings once. A surveillance team he doesn't recognize photographs him taking it. The beat is vertigo: he has crossed a line by simply showing up.

chapters.title: The Defector Who Smiles
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse waits in a safehouse, rehearsing her defection story, aware she is being watched by two different handlers who don't know about each other. She suspects she's bait but plays along because the evidence she carries is worth more than her life. The beat is controlled performance masking terror.

chapters.title: Terms of Translation
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Oscar's contact forces him onto the extraction team as interpreter, the only role plausible enough to move him across checkpoints. He realizes the delegation's 'peace' timeline exists to guarantee failure on schedule. The beat is complicity: he understands he has been translating his own betrayal for years.

chapters.title: What Casper Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Following Casper's dead-drop chain, Oscar finds recordings proving Casper anticipated his own murder and named the mole only as 'the inheritor.' The safehouse is burned mid-search; Oscar escapes with half the tape. The beat is desperate momentum and the first flicker of resolve.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV alternating Oscar/Ilse. The extraction convoy moves toward the border; Ilse tests Oscar in three languages, probing whether he's her escort or her executioner. Each wrong answer costs them a route. The beat is wary intimacy between two people who can only trust each other's lies.

chapters.title: The Inheritor
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Cornered at a rail yard, Oscar unmasks the mole: Deputy Head of Mission Aldous Renner, who inherited the sabotage operation from his father and treats the failed peace process as family estate. Renner offers Oscar survival in exchange for delivering Ilse. The beat is temptation priced in blood.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse learns definitively that she was offered up to draw out Casper's network, and that Oscar knew part of it. Instead of running, she proposes they reverse the trap: let Renner take her, while the real evidence travels another way. The beat is fury converted into strategy.

chapters.title: Crossing at Vellmar
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Climax at the border crossing: Renner takes the bait, Ilse is seized, and Oscar surrenders deliberately, using his interpreter status to get close enough to broadcast the recovered recording over the delegation's own channels. Casper appears alive in the crowd, refusing to help. The beat is sacrifice without rescue.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, coda Ilse. Ilse crosses with the evidence; the delegation collapses publicly; Oscar, disavowed and detained, finds Casper's final message: the inheritance was never the operation, it was the choice of what to carry across. Oscar chooses his name over his life. The beat is quiet, costly peace.
